measures.what_it_does: Authorizes Asotin County Rural EMS District No. 2 (the county outside Clarkston and Fire District 1: Anatone, Cloverland and south to Oregon) to levy a regular property tax for six years starting in 2027. The money pays for the county's contract with Lewiston Fire Department paramedics and ambulances. It replaces the levy that expires at the end of 2026. It failed in the August primary, 118 to 146, and is back for a second vote; a simple majority passes it.
measures.cost_line: Up to $0.28 per $1,000 of assessed value a year for 2027-2032, up from a current ceiling of $0.15 (the 2025 rate was about $0.12): $28 a year per $100,000 at the full rate.
measures.pro_summary: A group of rural residents says the levy pays for the advanced life support ambulance contract, cannot be used for other county expenses, and that without it EMS would stop when the Lewiston contract runs out. They say Life Flight is no substitute. The commissioners say they cannot advocate but have explained what it pays for.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition campaign was found. The measure nearly doubles the maximum EMS rate, and district voters rejected it with 55% voting no in August.

taxes.basis: A yes vote raises the district's regular EMS levy ceiling from $0.15 to $0.28 per $1,000 (the 2025 rate was about $0.12) for six more years.

measures.sources_note: Asotin local voters' pamphlet p. 12 (S1) and VoteWA guide record 7276 (S2); VoteWA August 2026 and SOS 2020 results (S3, S4); RCW 84.52.069 (S5); DOR 2025 levy detail and the county's 2025 tax rates (S6, S7); KOZE coverage (S8-S11, S13); supporters' letter (S12); PDC query (S14).
